headline: CAB Sets Level 17 Fuel Surcharge for October 1–15
seoTitle: CAB Sets Level 17 Fuel Surcharge for October 1–15 | FMB News
seoDescription: The Civil Aeronautics Board set a Level 17 fuel-surcharge ceiling for domestic and international flights from October 1 to 15, 2026.
deck: Airlines may apply to collect up to Level 17 from October 1 to 15, raising the passenger surcharge ceiling to ₱559–₱1,635 on domestic routes and ₱1,846.10–₱13,726.58 internationally.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Civil Aeronautics Board set Level 17 as the maximum passenger and cargo fuel surcharge airlines may collect for flights from October 1 to 15, 2026, up from Level 14 in the second half of September.
At Level 17, the passenger surcharge ranges from ₱559 to ₱1,635 for one-way domestic flights and from ₱1,846.10 to ₱13,726.58 for international flights, depending on distance.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The CAB advisory dated September 28 says airlines that want to impose the surcharge must apply with the Office of the Executive Director on or before the effectivity period. Level 17 is a ceiling, not an automatic charge on every ticket.

Independent transport publication PortCalls reported cargo caps of ₱2.87 to ₱8.40 per kilogram on one-way domestic flights and ₱9.49 to ₱70.57 per kilogram on one-way international flights originating in the Philippines. The CAB set the conversion rate at ₱62.71 per US dollar.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Travelers booking flights for the first half of October could face higher all-in fares if their airline applies for and collects the surcharge. Shippers may also see higher air-cargo costs, which can feed into logistics expenses.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Passengers should compare the full ticket price, not only the base fare, and check the carrier's fee breakdown before paying. The next 15-day CAB advisory will determine whether the ceiling changes after October 15.

verificationNotes: The CAB advisory was opened directly and confirms Level 17 for October 1–15, the application requirement, the ₱62.71 exchange rate, and the September 28 issue date.
PortCalls independently reported the Level 17 passenger and cargo ranges and the increase from Level 14.
PNA independently matched the passenger ranges and the CAB application requirement.
The article distinguishes the regulatory ceiling from an automatic charge: airlines must apply and may charge no more than Level 17.
The available publisher-owned airport photograph did not include reusable-rights documentation; FMB's owned editorial fallback is used and clearly labeled non-documentary.
